# Actual smoothing-scale normal motion and signed facet Bregman costs

This note uses actual minimizing cap normals, with the body held fixed. It retains the full finite displacement on the smoothing scale instead of only its Hessian. The same selected cap/body sequence is used throughout. It supplements, rather than automatically replaces, the transition-Hessian record at saturated selectors.

Use the compact positive-fiber setting and notation of `candidate 8bc6ff090380166a`. In particular h_l->0, the normalized actual minimizing caps N_l=(a_l,u_l), their sources Y_l, covariances Sigma_l and b_l=epsilon_l f_l(Y_l) converge, and Gamma_l(u_l)=1. Let

    q_l(w)=[N_l.(w-Y_l)+b_l]/h_l.

Only the uniform outward kernel is used. Let

    J(q)=integral_(-infinity)^q Psi(s) ds,
    B(q,s)=J(q+s)-J(q)-Psi(q)s >=0.

For each fixed bounded s, B is continuous in q on the compactified line [-infinity,+infinity], with value zero at both infinities. In fact it vanishes whenever the interval between q and q+s misses [-1,0]. Also 0<=B(q,s)<=|s|, so all following compactness passages have a uniform integrable bound.

## 1. An exact nonnegative residual at every width

First vary only the base tilt:

    a_l -> a_l+h_l t a',

and keep the cap through its SAME source. Its kernel argument changes EXACTLY to q_l+t k_l, where k_l(z)=a'.(z-p_l). At the actual minimizing cap, the first normal derivative vanishes:

    integral psi(q_l) k_l dmu_l=0.

Consequently for every real t the actual normal minimum gives

    R_l(t):=(1/h_l) integral
        [Psi(q_l+t k_l)-Psi(q_l)-t k_l psi(q_l)]dmu_l >=0.   (1)

This is an actual finite cap comparison; it is not inferred from a formal Taylor series and is not limited to a Hessian-null direction.

The same conclusion, with an error tending to zero on compact t intervals, holds for a full normal displacement N_l+h_l t D. Normalizing its continuous part changes the argument to

    q_l+t k_D,l+O(h_l),
    k_D,l=D.(w-Y_l)-gamma_D,l N_l.(w-Y_l).

The remainder is uniform on the compact bodies. Its effect on the integral is O(h_l^2), because the kernel can vary only in a strip of volume O(h_l); after division by h_l it vanishes. The first derivative still vanishes exactly. This accounts for BOTH buffer and width normalization, as in the Hessian note. Thus the limit below holds for every full normal variation D, with

    k_D(w)=D.(w-Y_bar), Y_bar=Y-b(0,Sigma u)

on the limiting cut plane. The test vanishes at Y_bar; no freely adjustable constant is present.

## 2. Proper cuts vanish and supporting cuts give opposite Bregman signs

The elementary one-dimensional identity underlying the limit is

    integral_(-infinity)^q
       [Psi(r+s)-Psi(r)-s psi(r)]dr = B(q,s).         (2)

Its integral over the whole real line is zero. Therefore a limiting PROPER fiber cut contributes zero to (1): coarea in the continuous normal direction gives a factor h_l, the section density and k_D,l converge uniformly on the bounded scaled transition interval to their values on the limiting proper section, and the remaining full-line integral is zero.

At a limiting OUTSIDE supporting facet, use the actual nearby upper roof in the direction of u_l. On each compact inner facet patch the body occupies normal coordinates from a uniformly remote lower endpoint to a roof with scaled kernel height q_l^F. Fubini and (2) give the positive contribution

    (1/|u|) integral_F B(q_l^F,t k_D) dH_(d-1)+o(1).

At INSIDE support, the body instead occupies the upper half-line from its boundary roof. Subtracting (2) from the zero full-line integral gives the NEGATIVE of the same expression. Normal directions and tangential coordinate changes converge; their Jacobians tend to one on compact inner patches.

Exhaustion of the full facet is justified by the bound B<=|t k_D| and convergence of the nearby section footprints. The omitted relative-boundary neighborhoods have arbitrarily small facet area. Lower-dimensional supporting contacts contribute zero by the same section-area bound. Thus there are no discarded boundary fibers or untracked positive-area contact pieces.

## 3. Retain the scaled offset record rather than guessing it from tau

On every supporting facet, retain a weak graph measure of the ACTUAL scaled boundary argument q_l^F, with values in [-infinity,+infinity]. Compactness gives a probability kernel nu_w(dq) over almost every facet point w. The graph measures have the ordinary facet area as their base marginal. Use a joint extraction for every finite selected cap, keeping source and inside/outside labels unchanged.

The uniform-kernel height theorem gives strong L1 convergence of the actual boundary captures. Hence

    nu_w is supported on {q:Psi(q)=W(w)},             (3)

where W=tau on OUTSIDE support and W=1-tau on INSIDE support. If 0<W<1, the record is the single finite value q=W-1. At W=0 or W=1 it can retain finite saturated offsets or an infinite offset. This is why tau alone is insufficient.

Since B(q,s) is continuous on this compactified offset space and bounded on compact s intervals, passing (1) yields, for EVERY real t and every full normal variation D,

    sum_out integral_F integral B(q,t k_D(w)) dnu_w(q)dH_(d-1)(w)
      >= sum_in integral_F integral B(q,t k_D(w)) dnu_w(q)dH_(d-1)(w).  (4)

The common factor 1/|u| has been canceled. A countable dense set of (t,D), followed by continuity and the uniform bound, gives ONE simultaneous record satisfying all these comparisons.

This is an exact signed convex-cost comparison on the actual transition facets. The local roof can diverge and its affine corrections can diverge. Their effect is kept in nu_w rather than replaced by an assumed finite profile.

The Bregman offset and the Hessian transition record can and should be extracted JOINTLY. In coordinates along u_l, the difference of the balanced endpoint footprints has density

    chi_l=1_{-1<q_l^F<0}+(1/2)1_{q_l^F=-1 or q_l^F=0}

on the roof footprint. The harmless area Jacobians tend to one. Retain the joint graph measure of (q_l^F,chi_l). Its conditional transition value is 1 when -1<q<0, is 0 when q lies outside [-1,0] (including both infinities), and may lie anywhere in [0,1] at the two corners. At corners this describes limits from either side as well as exact half traces; it does not force the value 1/2.

In particular the limiting Hessian density obeys

    chi(w)<=nu_w([-1,0])<=nu_w(R)=theta(w).           (4a)

Together with the support condition (3), this recovers chi=theta=1 on unsaturated selectors. It also prevents the Hessian and Bregman records from being assigned independently at saturated points. Both arise from the SAME roof and endpoint-footprint measures.

## 4. A selector-only necessary consequence and the limit-order caution

For a fixed W in [0,1], the largest B(q,s) among all q with Psi(q)=W occurs at the canonical endpoint value q=W-1. This is immediate for 0<W<1. For W=0, q<=-1 and convexity makes the largest possible transition cost occur at q=-1; for W=1, q>=0 and the largest occurs at q=0. Infinite offsets give zero.

On an unsaturated INSIDE patch q=-tau is fixed. Dropping all other nonnegative inside costs and bounding outside costs above gives the rigorous weaker consequence

    sum_out integral_F B(tau-1,t k_D)
        >= sum_in integral_(F intersect {0<tau<1}) B(-tau,t k_D).  (5)

The full offset-record inequality (4) is preferable whenever those records are available.

The Hessian and finite-displacement limits need not commute at saturated values. For example q_l=-1+1/l has tau_l->0 and transition Hessian density chi_l=1. Its finite-offset record tends to q=-1, whose CENTRAL second derivative has the balanced half value. Thus (4) does not automatically contain the separately retained Hessian constraint with its actual limiting chi. When the limiting offset record has no atoms at the two kernel corners, differentiating (4) twice at zero recovers the corresponding transition covariance inequality. In general both records should be kept.

The actual inside-transition example in `candidate be37e5b9b9c4c946` has q=-1/2 on both opposing facets, k values opposite, and B(-1/2,s)=B(-1/2,-s). It therefore satisfies (4) with equality as well as the Hessian equality. The exact all-base-tilt flat family there is consistent with this stronger test. No inside-selector elimination or Gamma_d/k payment follows without an additional geometric or minimal-body argument.

## 5. Linear costs on the finite-offset part, and comparison with the old quota

Let theta(w)=nu_w(R), the fraction of the retained offset record that is FINITE. For finite q,

    lim_(t->+infinity) B(q,t k)/t=[k]_+-Psi(q)k.

At q=+infinity or -infinity, B is identically zero for every finite t, so its limit is zero instead. Since B/|t|<=|k|, dominated convergence in the ALREADY TAKEN h-scale limit (4) proves

    sum_out integral_F theta([k_D]_+-tau k_D)
       >= sum_in integral_F theta([k_D]_+-(1-tau)k_D).  (6)

Replacing D by -D and adding gives

    sum_out integral_F theta |k_D|
       >= sum_in integral_F theta |k_D|.             (7)

No t/h interchange has been made. The finite-offset fraction equals one on unsaturated selectors and can be smaller on saturated selectors. This restriction is essential.

For comparison, there is also an OLD unrestricted absolute-incidence quota. At the limiting actual nonsmooth cap, its one-sided normal derivative is

    proper integral k_D
      +sum_out integral [k_D]_+
      +sum_in integral min(k_D,0) >=0.

The limit of the actual smooth first moment is

    proper integral k_D+sum_support integral tau k_D=0.

Subtracting gives the analogue of (6) with theta=1 on ALL supporting facets. Adding the two directions gives the corresponding unrestricted absolute-incidence quota. These formulas are the exact ordinary supporting-cap directional derivatives; they are not a new consequence of the h-scale analysis.

Thus the new information in (4), (6), and (7) is the shared, SCALE-SELECTED offset record and the full finite Bregman cost. Merely replacing a squared distance by an absolute distance, without retaining that selection, would reprove the older endpoint-support condition. Nor does equality in (4) imply that the positive-width cap is exactly flat along a finite interval of active base tilts: exact flatness requires equality of the original cap masses, not just equality after scaling and passage to a limit.
